Chapter 5. Parenting, Names, and the Search for Success.
Every parent wants the best for their kids, right? You read the books, ask for advice, and second-guess nearly every decision—what to feed them, which schools to pick, even what bedtime should look like. But let’s talk about one of the most personal choices of all: the name you give your child. We all hope it’ll open doors and set the stage for a bright future. But does it really make a difference?
Some parents believe that a unique or prestigious name will help their child stand out. Others worry that an unusual name could lead to teasing or even hold their child back. So, what does the research say? Well, it’s actually pretty surprising. While it’s true that certain names show up more often among successful people, the name itself usually isn’t the reason for their success.
Here’s the thing: names often reflect a family’s background and hopes for their child. For example, families with more resources and higher education tend to choose names that are popular in upper-class circles. But it’s not the name on the birth certificate that shapes the future—it’s the environment those families provide.
Of course, the choices parents make go far beyond names. There’s all the agonizing over bedtime routines, extracurricular activities, and whether you should read to your child every single night. We do all of this, hoping to give our kids every possible advantage. But when researchers dig into the data, they find that many of these worries—like how much TV your child watches or how strictly you enforce bedtime—actually have less impact than most people think.
What really counts are the things that aren’t as easy to change: your own education, your income, and how stable your home life is. These are the factors that shape your child’s opportunities and outlook in ways that bedtime stories or piano lessons just can’t match. That doesn’t mean parenting doesn’t matter—it absolutely does. But often, the most powerful influences are the ones we don’t even realize we’re passing on.
Imagine two families living in the same city. Both want the very best for their children. One family has access to great schools, safe neighborhoods, and a strong support network. The other faces tougher challenges—unstable jobs, crowded housing, and limited resources. Both sets of parents love their kids and work hard, but the opportunities their children have aren’t the same. And it’s those differences—far more than any single parenting decision—that shape what’s possible down the road.
It’s easy to search for the perfect formula for success. But the truth is, life is a mix of choices, circumstances, and a bit of luck. Parents try their best, but there are hidden forces at work that we just can’t control. By understanding what really matters, maybe we can focus on what we can change—and let go of some of that anxiety about being the perfect parent.
